A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Retrieval-of-Thought work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and matchable, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning experiments measuring accuracy, token usage, cost and latency, together with graph sensitivity, scalability and path-switching analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds experiments on additional model families, GPQA scientific reasoning and near-duplicate mathematical problems.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same graph construction, initial-node selection, reward-guided traversal, termination and template integration. The added experiments explicitly apply the existing procedure with different models or graph contents.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained AIME/AMC evaluations and Appendix B motivation tasks, Sections 5.5–5.6 add GPQA scientific reasoning and a near-duplicate retrieval scenario. The latter uses graphs built from numerically altered mathematical problems while evaluating original questions, substantially extending domain and input-condition coverage.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain CoT, CoT-SC, RAG and BoT. New studies compare RoT variants with the existing CoT baseline. DLER-7B and DeepSeek-R1-Llama8B are additional evaluated backbones, rather than newly introduced competing inference methods.

E3.justification: Section 5.4 adds DLER-7B and DeepSeek-R1-Llama8B evaluations on AMC 2023 and AIME 2024. Sections 5.5–5.6 introduce scientific-graph and variant-only-graph evaluation designs, including testing original questions against perturbed-example memory. The original Qwen3 evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.6 adds a dedicated robustness study across four Qwen3 sizes, testing whether retrieval confounds structurally similar problems with different constants or bounds. This examines a previously untested retrieval failure condition. Existing parameter sensitivity, graph-size ablations and path-switching analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C retains its existing uncertainty-band discussion and plots. New Tables 1–3 report point estimates without adding seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 add substantial new accuracy and token results; the original appendix values are unchanged. For example, DLER-7B on AIME 2024 reports 37.04% accuracy with CoT versus 51.85% with RoT+TI. Results also expose tradeoffs: GPQA Qwen3-14B RoT+TI reduces tokens by 51.1% but achieves 42.31% accuracy versus CoT's 57.69%.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–2, semantic-edge construction, edge weights, reward Equations 1–2 and the termination condition are unchanged. Neither the main text nor appendices add mathematical assumptions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about dynamic thought reuse, efficiency with preserved accuracy and broad applicability. The new experiments provide additional evidence for previously stated claims; the abstract's substantive addition is code-access information.

C2.justification: Sections 5.4–5.6 add interpretations of accuracy–length tradeoffs across model families, scientific-domain transfer and near-duplicate robustness attributed to abstract reasoning operations. These are localized extensions; the existing Discussion and Conclusion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 states that code is available and supplies a repository link in the abstract, whereas v1 only promises its release. It also briefly describes construction of the new experimental graphs. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware descriptions and example prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liu et al.'s DLER reference to support the additional model-family evaluation. Section 2 and Appendix A retain their prior-work discussion and positioning of dynamic thought composition relative to static-template approaches.

P1.justification: v2 inserts three experimental subsections and moves latency analysis after path-switching analysis. Affiliations, publication headers and acknowledgments are updated. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Three compact main-text tables are added. The latency and path-switching figures are relocated and renumbered, and original appendix Tables 1–6 become Tables 4–9. Existing visual designs are retained, with localized layout changes.

improvement.justification: The new studies strengthen direct validation beyond v1's Qwen3 mathematical evaluations and examine a relevant retrieval failure condition; the code link improves access information. The gain is limited by sparse documentation of the new datasets and graphs and absent uncertainty estimates. Favorable interpretations also underplay accuracy costs, such as GPQA Qwen3-14B RoT+TI falling from CoT's 57.69% to 42.31% accuracy despite saving tokens.
